about: main subject: primary topic of a work or act of communication
actor: cast member: actor in the subject production [use "character role" (P453) and/or "name of the character role" (P4633) as qualifiers] [use "voice actor" (P725) for voice-only role] - [use "recorded participant" (P11108) for non-fiction productions]
address: street address: full street address where subject is located. Include building number, city/locality, post code, but not country; use also P669 if the street has its own separate item
affiliation: affiliation: organization that a person or organization is affiliated with (not necessarily member of or employed by)
aggregateRating: review score: review score received by a creative work or other entity
alternateName: alternative name: qualifier for alternative name(s), given for a subject in a database entry, or preserved in references (even these are no longer the preferred name)
alumniOf: educated at: educational institution attended by subject
audience: intended public: intended audience or user of this work, product, object, or event
audio: audio: relevant sound. If available, use a more specific property. Samples: "spoken text audio" (P989), "pronunciation audio" (P443)
author: author: main creator(s) of a written work (use on works, not humans); use P2093 (author name string) when Wikidata item is unknown or does not exist
award: award received: award or recognition received by a person, organization or creative work
birthDate: date of birth: date on which the subject was born
birthPlace: place of birth: most specific known birth location of a person, animal or fictional character
brand: brand: commercial brand associated with the item
byArtist: performer: actor, musician, band or other performer associated with this role or musical work
character: character role: specific role played or filled by subject -- use only as qualifier of "cast member" (P161), "voice actor" (P725) | characters: characters which appear in this item (like plays, operas, operettas, books, comics, films, TV series, video games)
children: child: subject has object as child. Do not use for stepchildren—use "relative" (P1038), qualified with "kinship to subject" (P1039)
citation: cites work: citation from one creative or scholarly work to another
contentLocation: narrative location: the narrative of the work is set in this location
contributor: contributor to the creative work or subject: the value of this property is a person or organization that contributed to the subject or work
copyrightHolder: copyright holder: person or organisation who holds the copyright of a work according to the Berne Convention
countryOfOrigin: country of origin: country of origin of this item (creative work, food, phrase, product, etc.)
creator: creator: maker of this creative work or other object (where no more specific property exists)
deathDate: date of death: date on which the subject died
deathPlace: place of death: most specific known (e.g. city instead of country, or hospital instead of city) death location of a person, animal or fictional character
director: director: director(s) of film, TV-series, stageplay, video game or similar | director: director of a creative work
dissolutionDate: dissolved, abolished or demolished: point in time at which the subject (organisation, building) ceased to exist; see "date of official closure" (P3999) for closing a facility, "service retirement" (P730) for retiring equipment, "discontinued date" (P2669) for stopping a product
duns: D-U-N-S number: unique company identifier from Dun & Bradstreet
editor: editor: person who checks and corrects a work (such as a book, newspaper, academic journal, etc.) to comply with a rules of certain genre. Also applies to person who establishes the text of an ancient written work or manuscript.
email: email address: email address, prefixed with mailto:
encodingFormat: media type: IANA-registered identifier for a file type | file format: file format, compression type, or ontology used in a file
endDate: end time: moment when an entity ceases to exist and a statement stops being entirely valid or no longer be true
familyName: family name: part of full name of person
faxNumber: fax number: telephone number of a facsimile line
founder: founder: founder or co-founder of this organization, religion, place or entity
foundingLocation: location of formation: location where a group or organization was formed
gender: sex or gender: sex or gender identity of human or animal. For human: male, female, non-binary, intersex, transgender female, transgender male, agender, etc. For animal: male organism, female organism. Groups of same gender use subclass of (P279)
genre: genre: creative work's genre or an artist's field of work (P101). Use main subject (P921) to relate creative works to their topic
givenName: given name: first name or another given name of this person; values used with the property should not link disambiguations nor family names
hasCertification: has certification: states that an item has a certain certification
hasOccupation: occupation: occupation of a person. See also "field of work" (Property:P101), "position held" (Property:P39). Not for groups of people. There, use "field of work" (Property:P101), "industry" (Property:P452), "members have occupation" (Property:P3989).
hasPart: has part(s): part of this subject; inverse property of "part of" (P361). See also "has parts of the class" (P2670).
homeLocation: residence: the place where the person is or has been, resident
honorificPrefix: honorific prefix: word or expression used before a name, in addressing or referring to a person
honorificSuffix: honorific suffix: word or expression with connotations conveying esteem or respect when used, after a name, in addressing or referring to a person
icaoCode: ICAO airport code: four-character alphanumeric identifier for designating airports (for airlines, see P230)
illustrator: illustrator: person drawing the pictures or taking the photographs in a book or similar work
inLanguage: language of work or name: language associated with this creative work (such as books, shows, songs, broadcasts or websites) or a name (for persons use "native language" (P103) and "languages spoken, written or signed" (P1412))
isbn: ISBN-13: identifier for a book (edition), thirteen digit
issn: ISSN: International Standard Serial Number (print or electronic)
knowsLanguage: languages spoken, written or signed: language(s) that a person or a people speaks, writes or signs, including the native language(s)
leiCode: Legal Entity Identifier: identifier for a legally distinct entity per ISO 17442
locationCreated: location of creation: place where the item was conceived or made; where applicable, location of final assembly
material: made from material: material the subject or the object is made of or derived from (do not confuse with P10672 which is used for processes)
memberOf: member of: organization, club or musical group to which the subject belongs. Do not use for membership in ethnic or social groups, nor for holding a political position, such as a member of parliament (use P39 for that)
name: name: name the subject is known by; preferably use a more specific subproperty if available | name: name the subject is known by; preferably use a more specific subproperty if available
nationality: country of citizenship: the object is a country that recognizes the subject as its citizen
numTracks: number of parts of this work: the number of parts that a work comprises
numberOfEpisodes: number of episodes: number of episodes in a film/TV/radio series
numberOfPages: number of pages: number of pages in an edition of a written work; see allowed units constraint for valid values to use for units in conjunction with a number
numberOfSeasons: number of seasons: number of seasons a television or radio series has had
operatingSystem: operating system: operating system (OS) on which a software works or the OS installed on hardware
organizer: organizer: person or institution organizing an event
owns: owner of: entities owned by the subject
parentOrganization: parent organization or unit: parent organization or unit of an organization or unit, opposite of child organization or unit (P355); use instance of (P31) to distinguish organization (Q43229) and organization unit (Q10387680)
producer: producer: person(s) who produced the film, musical work, theatrical production, etc. (for film, this does not include executive producers, associate producers, etc.) [for production company, use P272, video games - use P178]
productionCompany: production company: company that produced this film, audio or performing arts work
provider: manufacturer: (main or final) manufacturer or producer of this product | collection: art, museum, archival, or bibliographic collection of which the subject is part (item is in the collection of X)
publisher: publisher: organization or person responsible for publishing a work, such as a book, periodical, printed music, podcast, game or software
recordedAt: recording location: location where a media item (sound, video, etc.) was recorded
sibling: sibling: the subject and the object have at least one common parent (brother, sister, etc. including half-siblings); use "relative" (P1038) for siblings-in-law (brother-in-law, sister-in-law, etc.) and step-siblings (step-brothers, step-sisters, etc.)
slogan: motto: description of the motto of the subject
sponsor: sponsor: organization or individual that sponsors this item
spouse: spouse: the subject has the object as their spouse (husband, wife, partner, etc.). Use "unmarried partner" (P451) for non-married companions
startDate: inception: time when an entity begins to exist; for date of official opening use P1619 | start time: time an entity begins to exist or a statement starts being valid
subOrganization: child organization or unit: child organization/unit of an org./unit; usually a fully owned separate org.; for non-independent sub-units, see org. division (P199); opposite of parent org./unit (P749); use instance of (P31) to distinguish org. (Q43229) and org. unit (Q10387680)
telephone: phone number: telephone number in standard format (RFC3966), without "tel:" prefix
track: tracklist: audio tracks contained in this release
translator: translator: agent who adapts any kind of written text from one language to another
video: video: relevant video; use property P18 for images; for film trailers, qualify with "object has role" (P3831)="trailer" (Q622550); for films, qualify with "object has role" (P3831)="full video available on Wikimedia Commons" (Q89347362)
workExample: has version, edition or translation: item that is an edition or translation of this item
worksFor: employer: person or organization for which the subject works or worked
